item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Front of a building with a car parked outside]

The car is 3.5 m long. About how long is the building?
item.figure_description: A line drawing showing the front facade of a single-story building. In the center is a double door with an arched window above it. Symmetrically flanking the doors are six identical rectangular windows with multipaned sashes: three windows to the left of the door and three to the right. Parked on the ground along the far left of the building facade is a black car, positioned spanning the space of roughly the first two windows. The length of the entire building is approximately four times the length of the car.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A workman cut off 1/5 of a pipe. The piece he cut off was 3 meters long.

How many meters long was the original pipe?
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A ruler with a wavy string above it]

If the string in the diagram is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description: A metric ruler marked from 0 to 11 cm, with ticks at every centimeter and half-centimeter, labeled 'cm' at the left end and with numbers 1 through 11. Above the ruler, a curved line labeled 'string' begins at the 3 cm mark, extends horizontally to approximately 5.5 cm, loops back leftward to about 4.7 cm, and then extends horizontally rightward, ending near the 7 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A rectangular garden that is next to a building has a path around the other three sides, as shown.

[Image: Diagram of a garden and path next to a building]

What is the area of the path?
reference_items.figure_description: A diagram shows a thick line labeled "Building" forming a vertical wall. Directly adjacent to the building wall is a shaded rectangular "Garden", surrounded on the remaining three sides by an unshaded "Path" forming a larger outer rectangle. The dimensions shown are: total vertical height of the outer rectangle along the building wall is 12 m; horizontal length of the garden is 10 m; vertical height of the garden is 8 m; and total horizontal width of the outer rectangle (garden plus path width) along the bottom is 12 m.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A ruler measuring the length of a pipe]

What is the length of the pipe being measured?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal ruler labeled "Meters (m)" at the top has major tick marks from 0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.1, with minor tick marks halfway between each major tick mark (representing increments of 0.05). Below the ruler, a gray cylindrical pipe is positioned horizontally. Dimension lines with arrows indicate the length being measured from the left end of the pipe, which aligns with 0 on the ruler, to the right end of the pipe, which aligns with the tick mark halfway between 0.8 and 0.9.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
On the map, 1 cm represents 10 km on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and roads]

On the land, about how far apart are the towns Melville and Folley?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangular map showing three towns marked with dots: Melville near the top center, Mockem on the middle left, and Folley to the lower right. A thick curved black line representing "Red River" runs diagonally across the map from the lower-left to the upper-right. Thin lines represent roads: one goes vertically down through Melville and Mockem, and another connects Melville curving down and to the right, crossing the Red River and passing through Folley. In the bottom right corner of the map, an inset box contains a scale line segment marked with vertical end-ticks labeled "1 cm = 10 km". On the map, the straight-line distance between Melville and Folley is approximately 5 times the length of the 1 cm scale bar.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A graph of car production with time on the x-axis and total number of cars produced on the y-axis. Time starts at 8 a.m. and goes to 4 p.m. in one hour increments. Total number of cars produced goes from 0 to 400 in intervals of 50. A straight dotted line is drawn on the graph, going from the origin at 0 cars at 8 a.m., to the top right of the graph, at 4:00p.m. and 400 cars. A solid line is shown starting at the origin and going above the dotted line after 8:00a.m. and before 11:30 a.m. The solid line then goes below the dotted line from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. It again goes above the dotted line from 1:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. and ends at 400 cars at 4:00 p.m. At 150 total cars produced, the solid line is at 10a.m. and the dotted line is at 11:00a.m.]

The solid line (——) on the graph shows car production by the NU Car Motor Company during a particular day.

The dotted line (-----) shows what the total number of cars produced would be if the rate of production were constant.

A. By what time had a total of 150 cars been produced?

Answer: ____

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Two horizontal pipes]

The first pipe is x meters long. The second pipe is y times as long as the first one. How long is the second pipe?
reference_items.figure_description: Two horizontal cylindrical pipes arranged end-to-end horizontally. The first pipe on the left is shorter, with a rounded left end, an oval opening at the right end, and the label "x meters" inside. The second pipe on the right is longer, with a rounded left end, an oval opening at the right end, and no label.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Number line from 0 to 3 with a point P marked]

What is the best estimate of the number corresponding to P?

On the line between 1 and 2, slightly to the right of 1 (at approximately one-fifth of the distance from 1 to 2), there is a solid black point labeled "P" directly above it.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
